title: Brigadeirão - Brazilian Chocolate Flan
ldKeywords: brigadeiro, brigadeiro recipe, chocolate, flan, flan recipe
ldIngredientsRaw: 200 grams of semi-sweet chocolate bar (50-56% cacao)  (*see notes )
470 milliliters of heavy cream (milk cream that has between 36-40% fat)
Good quality chocolate sprinkles, for topping (about two cups)
ldInstructionsRaw: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) for a fan-assisted convection oven, or 200°C (400°F) for a conventional oven.
Butter the bundt pan using a paper towel, then sprinkle with sugar and shake to coat all sides. Place the prepared bundt pan inside a large roasting pan. Set aside.

Cut up the chocolate into smaller pieces and add them to a medium-sized microwave-safe bowl. Add a splash of the heavy cream (about 2 tablespoons) and microwave in 30-second increments, stirring until it's all melted and smooth.

Add the condensed milk, the remaining cream, and melted chocolate to the base of a blender and blend until fully smooth. Scrape the sides of the blender as needed to fully incorporate all the ingredients.
Add the eggs all at once and pulse just until incorporated (about three 10-second pulses or until everything is incorporated).

Pour the custard into the prepared bundt pan. If using a convection oven, add hot tap water to the larger pan until halfway up the sides of the bundt pan. If using a conventional oven, use boiling water instead. Cover the bundt pan with foil, poke 4 holes in the foil, and bake at the preheated-temperature for 15 minutes, then reduce to 150°C (300°F) for convection or 175°C (325°F) for conventional, and bake for a further 1 hour and 15 minutes. The flan will still jiggle a little at the center when done. It will firm up as it cools.**
Let the cooked flan rest in the hot water bath on the counter for another 1 hour. The residual heat will continue to cook the flan as it rests there.

After that hour, loosen the flan from the sides of the pan by running a paring knife around the inside and the outside rims. Then place plastic wrap over the flan and refrigerate in the pan for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight.

To cleanly unmold the flan, place the bundt pan into a hot water bath for about 30 seconds. You're looking for that hardened fat on the edges of the flan to turn transparent, which means it's melting and releasing the flan from the pan. Give the pan a gentle shake or wiggle. You'll feel the flan start to move. Place your serving plate over the pan and flip it with confidence. It should release easily.
Wipe off excess syrup with a paper towel if desired, then top generously with chocolate sprinkles. Slice, serve and enjoy!
